newsitem.title: UK: No solace for owners in Ldn freight fixtures.
newsitem.headline: No solace for owners in Ldn freight fixtures.

text.p: Nothing in Thursday's dry cargo freight market signalled a rescue for the owners from their present misery, shipbrokers said.

The Baltic Freight Index fell eight more points to 1003 to equal a level not seen since August 5, 1987. Owners are being squeezed by a number of different negative factors whose combined effect is producing a serious slump.

The most discouraging feature of all for the industry is the generally poor level of chartering demand worldwide. It is true that the volume of fixtures remains reasonably good but rates are almost universally soft and in some areas are continuing to decline.

Much will depend on the forthcoming North American grain crop to boost the freight market but in the meantime the only serious positive news involving this commodity concerns reports that Saudi interests have bought 1.7 million tonnes of barley to be shipped from Europe in October and November.

Meanwhile the outlook for Capers for October in the Atlantic in particular is unpromising with little business available from USEC or Brazil. Prospects from Richards Bay and Australia appear better but it is believed that about 45 newbuilding Capers are scheduled for delivery before the end of March next year.

Together with estimates of newbuilding Panamaxes being delivered at twice this rate and reports that owners are finding difficulty selling old tonnage for scrap in the Far East, the outlook for the freight rate is discouraging, brokers said.

Dreyfus fixed the 1977-built Finix of 5,372,000 cft grain from Port Cartier to Rotterdam for Sept/Oct dates at a lumpsum of $560,000. Another very weak rate was seen in the Continent/ Saudi Arabia trade with Glencore booking 1974-built obo Monterey for 60,000 barley at $14.00 basis two ports N france - Brokers estimate loading port disbursements alone in the region of $150,000 for this business.

Halla have fixed 50/55,000 rye from Rostock or Hamburg to Japan for oct 25 on private terms. Brokers believe the rate was close to $19.00. Otherwise news was thin in the grain market, especially regarding fresh business. Cargill shifted their order of 55,000/5 wheat to Egypt for Oct 5/10 from US Gulf to Baie Comeau loading, indicating $7.75.

China Steel fixed Hadera for 120,000/10 ironore Sepetiba/Kaohsiung for first half Nov at $9.00 and were also linked with Cape Europe for a similar quantity and dates from Tubarao at $8.80 or PDM at $9.15. Reports circulated of Portland Star 150,661 dwt having been fixed by Docenave delivery prompt Continent for a Brazil round redelivery UK at $10,750 daily, although some brokers suspected the business was done last week.

Hoogovens were said to have fixed Docecape for 140,000/10 ironore PDM/Ijmuiden at $4.50. Cape Kestrel 160,849 dwt was rumoured fixed in the East for backhaul business. One of the few relatively firm fixtures reported Thursday was a 1994-blt 75,000 dwt Panamax vessel delivery Brazil Sept/Oct trip Far East with ironore at $10,600 daily plus $200,000 bonus for account of Japanese charterers, possibly K Line.

A fair reflection of conditions in the Atlantic was a report that Aktea 43,841 dwt ballasted from USEC to the Continent to fix scrap for account of Glencore to S Korea at a lumpsum equivalent in the region of $28.00. A further decline in timecharter rates in the craned bulker category was seen with PanOcean's fixture of Tai Shan Hai 47,665 dwt delivery Skaw Oct 10/15 trip Far East at only $10,400 daily. Elsewhere conditions for handies, especially in the Far East and South Atlantic, have been very quiet.
